en:
נָתַן (Biblical Hebrew) to give; to place, put. Gittin I, 6 תֵּן גט וכ׳ give this letter of divorce to my wife. Ib. תְּנוּ גט וכ׳ give ye &c. Ib. לא יִתְּנוּ לאחר מיתה they must not deliver it after the man’s death; and see from—נשא ונ׳, see נָשָׂא.—נ׳ עיניו ל (to put an eye upon) to intend. Bava Metzia 19ᵃ, and e. כיון שנ׳ ע׳ לגרשה as soon as he has resolved to divorce her; and from—נ׳ עיניו ב (to have an eye on) to desire, think of. Nedarim XI, 12 שלא תהא אשה נוֹתֶנֶת עיניה באחר lest the woman have a liking for another man. Ib. 20ᵇ שלא אֶתֵּן עיני וכ׳ lest I think of another woman. Ib. אל ישתה … ויִתֵּן וכ׳ one must not drink of one cup (have connection with one woman) and think of another; and from—Esp. נ׳ עיניו בו to cast an angry eye at, to hurt by an angry look. Berakhot 58ᵃ נ׳ ע׳ בו ונעשה וכ׳ he cast an eye at him and he was changed into &c., see גַּל; Shabbat 34ᵃ; and e.—Yerushalmi Berakhot III, beginning 5ᵈ, and from נוֹתן תפלין puts on T’fillin.—נ׳ טעם, see טַעַם.—הדין נותן the conclusion ad majus gives it, it is a legitimate conclusion. Bekhoroth 59ᵇ, and from Ib. היא הנוֹתֶנֶת (on the contrary,) it is thus we should argue.—Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 33 והדין נותן and it stands to reason.—Esp. נ׳ (subaudi דם) to put blood on the altar, sprinkle, smear. Zevachim VIII, 4; and from—[Tosefta Negaim VI, 10 נותן, see נָתַץ.]

Nifal - נִיתַּן to be given, put &c.; to be intended. Nedarim 38ᵃ לא נִיתְּנָה תורה אלא וכ׳ the Law was given only to Moses and his descendants. Ib. וכולן נִתְּנוּ וכ׳ and all those (gates of understanding) were granted to Moses; and from—Ketubot 81ᵃ לא ניתנה כתובה וכ׳ the K’thubah is not intended to be collected during life-time. Rosh Hashanah 28ᵃ מצות … נִיתְּנוּ, see הָנָה; and from—[Tosefta Pirkei Avot Zar. V (VI), 8 עד שינתן, see נָתַץ.]—Esp. to be put on the altar, sprinkled, smeared. Zevachim VIII, 9 הנִתָּנִין למטה … בנתנין למעלה blood which must be put below (the red line) which has been mixed with blood that must be put above. Ib. 10 יִנָּתְנוּ במתן וכ׳ shall be applied four times, see מַתָּן and מַתָּנָה; and from

Hof. - הוּתָּן to be put. Makhshirin I, 1 בכי יוּתַּן (הרי זה) it comes under the law (Vayikra XI, 38), i.e. it is a liquid which, if put on eatables, makes them susceptible of uncleanness. Ib. 2 אינן בכי יותן do not qualify for uncleanness; and from

רָצוֹן m. (Biblical Hebrew; רָצָה) desire, will, good-will. Midrash Tanḥuma Ki Thissa 27 כשאהיה אני עליהם אתה הוי בר׳ … אני בר׳ when I am angry with them, be thou in a conciliatory mood; and when thou art angry, I will be conciliatory, see רָצָה. Pirkei Avot II, 4 עשה רְצוֹנוֹ כרְצוֹנְךָ וכ׳ do his (God’s) will as being thy will, in order that he may do thy desire as being his own; בטל רצונך וכ׳, see בָּטֵל I. Tosefta Berakhot III, 7 עשה רצונך וכ׳ do thou thy will in the heavens above; Berakhot 29ᵇ; and see from—יהי ר׳ (abbrev. יה"ר) be it the will (of God), see רַעֲוָא. Ib. 28ᵇ. Taanit 5ᵇ, sq.; and see from—יהי ר׳ מלפניך (abbrev. יר"מ) be it thy will. Berakhot 60ᵃ; and from—בר׳ willingly, opposed באונס. Ketubot 9ᵃ; and from—לר׳ a) acceptable. Sifra Vayikra, N’dab., Chaldaic III, Parah 3 (reference. to Vayikra I, 3) כשם שאם אינו תמים אינו לר׳ וכ׳ as a sacrifice is not acceptable when it is not perfect &c.; and e.—b) intentionally. Makhshirin VI, 8 מטמא לר׳ ושלא לר׳ makes susceptible of uncleanness whether it is discharged intentionally (by milking) or unintentionally (by spontaneous dripping); ib. המשקין … לר׳ the liquids which come out of them with man’s intention (by pressing); Shabbat 143ᵇ, sq.; and from—c) welcome. Makhshirin I, 1 כל משקה שתחלתו לר׳ וכ׳ a liquid the contact with which is welcome at first (e.g. rain washing utensils), though finally it may be unwelcome (injurious).

comments.en: but if water is put on the seed and any part of a carcass falls upon it, it shall be unclean for you.
comments.he: וְכִ֤י יֻתַּן־מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־זֶ֔רַע וְנָפַ֥ל מִנִּבְלָתָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם׃ {ס}

sections.en: Any liquid which was desired at the beginning though it was not desired at the end, or which was desired at the end though it was not desired at the beginning, comes under the law of "if water be put." Unclean liquids render unclean whether [their action] is desired or is not desired.
sections.he: כָּל מַשְׁקֶה שֶׁתְּחִלָּתוֹ לְרָצוֹן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין סוֹפוֹ לְרָצוֹן, אוֹ שֶׁסּוֹפוֹ לְרָצוֹן אַף עַל פִּי שֶׁאֵין תְּחִלָּתוֹ לְרָצוֹן, הֲרֵי זֶה בְכִי יֻתַּן. מַשְׁקִין טְמֵאִים מְטַמְּאִין לְרָצוֹן וְשֶׁלֹּא לְרָצוֹן:

en:
רָעַד (Biblical Hebrew) to tremble.

Hifil - הִרְעִיד to shake. Makhshirin I, 2, sq. המַרְעִיד את האילן if one shakes a tree; Tosefta ib. I, 1, sq.—[Sifré Bamidbar 11 ומרעדים את העין. see עִרְעֵר II.]

sections.en: If one shook a tree in order to cause food or something unclean to fall down from it, [the rain water dropping down from it] does not come under the law of ‘if water be put.' If [he shook the tree] in order to cause liquids to fall down from it: Bet Shammai says: both [the liquids] that fall down and [the liquids] that remain [on the tree] come under the law of ‘if water be put.' But Bet Hillel say: [the liquids] that fall down come under the law of ‘if water be put’, but [the liquids] that remain [on the tree] do not come under the law of ‘if water be put,' because his intention was that [the liquids] should drop down from all the tree.
sections.he: הַמַּרְעִיד אֶת הָאִילָן לְהַשִּׁיר מִמֶּנּוּ אֳכָלִין אוֹ אֶת הַטֻּמְאָה, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. לְהַשִּׁיר מִמֶּנּוּ מַשְׁקִין, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, הַיּוֹצְאִין וְאֶת שֶׁבּוֹ, בְּכִי יֻתַּן. בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, הַיּוֹצְאִין, בְּכִי יֻתַּן, וְאֶת שֶׁבּוֹ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּוֵּן שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ מִכֻּלּוֹ:

en: חֲלִיקוּפְרִי, חֲלִי קוּפְרִי m. (patron. of Σόλοι Κύπριοι) one from Soloe (Aligora), a sea-port town of Cyprus. Makhshirin I, 3 Abba José ח׳ איש טבעון Arukh (ed. two words) of Soloe, a citizen of Tibon.

טִבְעוֹן, טִבְעִין, טִי׳, (טִבְעִים) proper noun of a place Tibon or Tibin (probably Tubun, west of Sepphoris, Neubauer Géographie du Talmud, Paris 1868 p. 196). Makhshirin I, 3, see חֲלִיקוּפְרִי.—Tosefta Megillah II, 5; Yerushalmi ib. IV, beginning 74ᶜ בה"כ של טיבעין the synagogue of T.—Sifré Devarim 323 איש טיבעים; Yalkut Devarim 946 כפר טיבעין.—[Eruvin 29ᵃ bottom of page לטיבעין (Variant טביעים, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 6), missing in Tosefta ib. IX (VI), 4, see עַרְדִּיסְקוֹס.]

סוֹכָה, שׂ׳ (Biblical Hebrew שׂוֹכָה) = סוֹךְ. Makhshirin I, 3. Yerushalmi Shabbat XV, end, 15ᵇ. Bava Metzia 105ᵇ, see חִזָּיוֹן II. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 15 מס׳ לס׳ from bush to bush; Shir HaShirim Rabbah to II, 9; Yalkut ib. 986. Pirkei Avot d’R. N. Chaldaic XXXIX קוצו ס׳ זו וכ׳ cut this limb off the tree. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 10, beginning הס׳ הזו של קוצים (not הזה) this thorn-bush. Tosefta Eruvin XI (VIII), 11 (not סיכה), see סוֹךְ. Eicha Rabbah to V, 13 בש׳ אחת, see חָרַז; and e.—plural סוֹכוֹת. Yerushalmi Beitzah IV, 62ᶜ top ס׳ תאנים, see סוֹךְ.

comments.en: but if water is put on the seed and any part of a carcass falls upon it, it shall be unclean for you.
comments.he: וְכִ֤י יֻתַּן־מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־זֶ֔רַע וְנָפַ֥ל מִנִּבְלָתָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם׃ {ס}

sections.en: If one shook a tree and it fell on another tree, or a branch and it fell on another branch, and under them were seeds or vegetables [still] joined to the ground: Bet Shammai say: this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’. But Bet Hillel say: this does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’. R. Joshua said in the name of Abba Yose Holikofri a man of Tivon: Be surprised if there is any liquid that according to the Torah causes susceptibility to uncleanness except one put it on with intention, for it is said: "If water be put upon the seed."
sections.he: הַמַּרְעִיד אֶת הָאִילָן וְנָפַל עַל חֲבֵרוֹ, אוֹ סוֹכָה וְנָפְלָה עַל חֲבֶרְתָּהּ, וְתַחְתֵּיהֶן זְרָעִים אוֹ יְרָקוֹת הַמְחֻבָּרִין לַקַּרְקַע, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן. בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ מִשּׁוּם אַבָּא יוֹסֵי חֲלֵי קוּפְרִי אִישׁ טִבְעוֹן, תְּמַהּ עַצְמְךָ אִם יֵשׁ מַשְׁקֶה טָמֵא בַתּוֹרָה, עַד שֶׁיִּתְכַּוֵּן וְיִתֵּן, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר (ויקרא יא), וְכִי יֻתַּן מַיִם עַל זֶרַע:

en: גֵּיף m. (Biblical Hebrew גַּף) side, shore. Makhshirin I, 4 על ג׳ הנהר Arukh (ed. גַּב, R. Hai Gaon גַּף, see Kohelet Arukh Compl. section (Parashah) see note 9).

גַּב m. (Biblical Hebrew; גבב) convex, arched, whence
1) the exterior or upper part of a thing, a) body, especially back (of an animal’s body, usually אָחוֹר). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 8, beginning he split the double-faced body (see פרצוף) ועשאו גַּבַּיִים ג׳ לכאן וכ׳ and gave it two backs, one back on this side &c.—גַּב יָד, גַּב רֶגֶל a swelling on the hand, on the foot. Pirkei Avot Zar. 28ᵃ; Shabbat 109ᵃ.—b) eye-brow (Biblical Hebrew), the elevation around genitals &c. Niddah 52ᵇ א׳ בגַבָּהּ one hair on the lower surrounding of her genitals, opposed בכריסה, see כֶּרֶס; Bava Batra 56ᵇ; Sanhedrin 30ᵇ; Bava Kamma 70ᵇ, [Rashi: on her finger joints].—c) (also גַּבָּה) גַּבַּת הַזָּקֵן, plural גַּבּוֹת, chin. Niddah 23ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. III, 50ᶜ bottom of page גומות הזקן (dimples).—*d) a low fence. Tosefta Bava Metzia XI, 22 (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) גַּג).—Dual גַּבַּיִים, גַּבַּיִין. Kelim XXV, 5 outsides of vessels (usually אֲחוֹרַיִים). Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 8, see supra.—plural גַּבִּים, גַּבִּין, גַּבּוֹת. Bekhoroth VII, 2 שני ג׳ וכ׳ double back and double spine (explain. גִּבֵּן, Vayikra XXI, 20); Niddah 24ᵃ sq.; Chullin 60ᵇ.—Niddah 23ᵇ ג׳ הזקן, see supra.—עַל גַּב, עַל גַּבֵּי (abbr. ע"ג) on, upon, by the side of (compare עַל in Biblical Hebrew). Chullin 3ᵃ, and from עומד על גַּבָּיו standing by him, superintending. Niddah 66ᵃ על גב הנהר by the river-side; Makhshirin I, 4 (see גֵּיף). Sukkah IV, 4 על גב איצטבא (Talmud ed. 42ᵇ גבי), see אִיסְטְבָא.—Transferred on the basis, on the principle. אף על גב, see אַף I.—Yerushalmi Chagigah II, 78ᵇ bottom of page חולין שנעשו על גב הקדש (usually על טהרת הקדש) layman’s food prepared on the principles of sacred food (as though it were sacred food). Beitzah II, 3 (17ᵇ); Tosefta ib. II, 7 מטבילין מגב לגב you may (on a Holy Day) immerse vessels for the purpose of changing their use (literally: from principle to principle, from one על גב to another); explained ibid. רצה לעשות גיתו ע"ג בדו ובדו ע"ג עיסתו הרי זה וכ׳ if one desires to work his wine press on the basis of his olive press, i.e. with vessels originally immersed for the use of the olive press, or his olive press on the basis of his dough, i.e. with vessels originally immersed to be used for kneading, he may immerse his vessels on the same day; Beitzah 19ᵃ ע"ג בדו ובדו ע"ג גיתו עושה … Manuscript Munich and Arukh (ed. incorr. כדו) if one wishes to change &c., he might have done so (even without another immersion and, therefore, may re-immerse his vessels on the Holy Day because he does not thereby create a new status).—Cmp. אַגַּב.—Tosefta Shabbat XII (XIII), 1; Yerushalmi ib. XIII, 14ᵃ top ע"ג הגס וכ׳ around, or adding to the border of a web &c.; Bavli ib. 105ᵃ על הגס. Horayot III, 3 אין על גַּבָּיו אלא וכ׳ none over him save the Lord his God.—בְּגַב in the back, behind. Yerushalmi Ketubot XII, 35ᵇ top דברים בגב (Bavli ib. 111ᵃ בגו) there is something behind, i.e. there is a reason for it.—Cmp. כַּף.

נָעַר II (Biblical Hebrew; compare עור, ערר) to shake, stir. Makhshirin I, 4 הנוֹעֵר אגודה וכ׳ he who shakes (the rain off) a bundle of vegetables. Ib. V, 7. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 26 לאיוב נָעַרְתִּי מן האשפה וכ׳ I shook Job (making him rise) from the dunghill, and concerning thee (Israel) it is written (Isaiah LII, 2), shake thyself &c.; and e.

Piël - נִיעֵר
1) to shake. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana Shekalim, p. 17ᵃ נַעֲרָהּ קפלה shake it (the garment), fold it; Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 2. Bava Metzia II, 8 מצא כסות מְנַעֲרָהּ וכ׳ if one found a garment (and holds it in charge waiting for the owner to claim it), he must shake it once in thirty days. Shabbat 147ᵃ top; and from

—2) to stir. Chullin VIII, 3 נ׳ את הקדרה if he stirred (the meat in) the pot. Yerushalmi Pirkei Avot Zar. I, 39ᵈ top שמא נ׳ הגוי בקדרה the gentile might have stirred the pot; and from

—3) to empty; to cause evacuation. Toharot II, 1 מְנָעֶרֶת את הקדרה she may empty (or stir) the dish. Kelim XXVIII, 2 לנָעֵר בו וכ׳ used for (lifting and) emptying the pot. Tosefta Kelim Bava Metzia II, 10 שהחנוני מְנָעֵר וכ׳ which the shop-keeper uses when pouring out &c. (or through which he pours for straining), see יַתִּיךְ; and e.—נ׳ את הצאן to use means by which to expedite the discharge of excrements of the flock on the spot to be manured (see דּוּר I, Piël). Tosefta Sheviit II, 20; Moʿed Katan 12ᵃ; Yerushalmi Sheviit III, 34ᶜ bottom of page Ib. השוכר … לנַעֲרָהּ he who hires a flock (for manuring) is forbidden to use means &c.; explained ib. מוליכה ממקום וכ׳ by driving it from place to place.—Part. pass. מְנוֹעָר; f. מְנוֹעֶרֶת; plural מְנוֹעָרִים, מְנוֹעָרִין: מְנוֹעָרוֹת empty, vacant. Yerushalmi Berakhot IV, 7ᵇ bottom of page (play on שִׁנְ֗עָ֗ר̇) שחם מנ׳ מן המצות וכ׳ they (the Babylonians) are vacant of (cannot perform) certain religious observances &c.; Kohelet Rabbah to XII, 7; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 37 שהיא מנ׳ וכ׳ she (Babylonia) is deprived &c. Chagigah 14ᵃ (play on נערים, Isaiah III, 4) אלו בני אדם שמנ׳ וכ׳ that means persons empty of good deeds, opposed ממולא; Yalkut Isaiah 261.—[Bava Batra 74ᵇ ור"י נוער some ed., see עוּר I.—Chullin 51ᵇ ניערה, see infra.]

Nifal - נִנְעַר
1) to be stirred up; to bestir one’s self. Bava Batra 74ᵇ וני׳ ר׳'א and R. El. was stirred up (awoke). Sotah 5ᵃ אין עפרו נ׳ his dust will not be stirred up (for resurrection). Shemot Rabbah section (Parashah) 1 (play on חלאה ונערה, I Chr. IV, 5) חלתה ונִנְעֲרָה מחליה וכ׳ she (Miriam) was sick, but she bestirred herself (arose) from her sickness, and the Lord restored her to youth. Yerushalmi Berakhot III, 6ᵈ top (play on מנעריו, Breishit VIII, 21) משעה שהוא נ׳ ויוצא וכ׳ from the moment the embryo bestirs itself to come out into the world; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 34; Yalkut ib. 61. Chullin 51ᵇ ננערה לעמוד וכ׳ Rashi (ed. נִיעֲרָה) if the animal made an effort to get up, although it did not succeed; and e.

—2) (of flax) to be hatcheled. Yerushalmi Shabbat II, beginning 4ᶜ (explained חוסן, ib. II, 1) פשתן שלא ננערה flax which has not yet been hatcheled.

—3) to be emptied, poured out. Yerushalmi Berakhot l. common gender. (play on שנער) ששם נִנְעֲרוּ וכ׳ for into that valley the dead of the generation of the flood were dumped; Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 37; Kohelet Rabbah l. common gender.—Sanhedrin 92ᵃ קשתו נִינְעֶרֶת his bow will be empty (his sexual vitality broken).

Hifil - הִנְעִיר to stir up, to keep awake. Eruvin 53ᵇ (play on נערה &c., see אַהֲרוֹנִית) והִנְעִירָתוֹ and she kept him awake.

Hithpaël - הִתְנַעֵר to be emptied; trnsf. to be displaced. Zevachim 116ᵃ (reference. to Song of Songs IV, 16) תִּתְנַעֵר אומה … ותבא וכ׳ (see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note) removed be the (Roman) nation whose sacrifices are slaughtered northward (Vayikra I, 11, which is entitled only to burnt-offerings), and let the nation enter &c.

עוּד (Biblical Hebrew; compare עָדָה) to turn, return, occur; to continue, endure, exist (see Ges. Thes. section (Parashah) see).—Denom. עַד, עוֹד, עֵת &c.

Polel. - עוֹדֵד to straighten, erect, help up. Midrash Till. to Psalms CXLVI, 9 וכי כל … מְעוֹדֵד does the Lord uphold all widows and orphans?—*Part. pass. מְעוֹדָד; plural מְעוֹדָדִים, מְעוֹדָדִין. Tosefta Makhshirin I, 3 שק אחד מע׳ (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) מעודר, Variant מועדר; Rabbenu Shimshon to Makhshirin I, 4 מעורר; Makhshirin l. common gender. מלא פירות) one bag standing upright (closely packed); ib. שני שקין מע׳ (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) מעודרון, Variant מעודדי, Rabbenu Shimshon מעוררין).

Hifil - הֵעִיד (denominative of עֵד)
1) to declare one’s presence at a certain occurrence, especially to establish a law from a witnessed precedent or traditional knowledge. Eduy. II, 1 ר׳ חנינא … ה׳ וכ׳ R. H. … related four things which he knew by tradition. Ib. 3 אף הוא ה׳ על וכ׳ he also reported as a precedent the case of a small village &c.; and from

—2) to testify before court. Ib. IV, 11 מי שהיו … מְעִידוֹת אותו he concerning whom there were two sets of witnesses testifying; אלו מְעִידִים וכ׳ the ones testifying that &c. Makkot I, 1 מעידין אנו באיש … שגירש וכ׳ (Bavli ed. 3ᵃ … את איש) we testify about this man that he divorced &c. Ib. 2, sq.; and see from—Chagigah 5ᵃ וממהר להָעִידוֹ and is quick to testify against him; Yalkut Malachi 589 ומֵעִיד בו.

—3) to call upon as witness. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 2 מְעִידֵנִי עלי וכ׳ I call upon heaven and earth as my witnesses &c.; Arakhin 16ᵇ מעיד אני וכ׳; and from

—4) to forewarn, exhort. Vayikra Rabbah l. common gender. שבעה נביאים … והן מעידין וכ׳ seven prophets stood up for the nations exhorting them; לא הֵעִידוּ בנו they have not warned us; גירי הדור מעידין בדור the proselytes of every generation are an exhortation to their respective generation; and e.—Esp. to forewarn the owner of a noxious animal; to declare an animal noxious (see מוּעָד). Bava Kamma II, 4 כל שהֵעִידוּ בו וכ׳, see מוּעָד. Ib. 24ᵃ עד שיָעִידוּ בו וכ׳ unless he be declared noxious (testimony be deposited stating the facts on which the declaration is based) in the presence of the owner and in court. Ib. הֵעִידוּהוּ שנים וכ׳ if the first case has been ascertained by two witnesses &c.; and from—Part. pass. מוּעָד see as well
שפקין , Tosefta Makhshirin I, 2, read: שעִקְּרָן (see Rabbenu Shimshon to Makhshirin I, 4).

comments.he: אמרו ב"ה לב"ש הכל מודין במעלה מעודד ונתנו על גב הנהר שאע"פ שהמים יורדים מצד העליון לתחתון שאינן בכי יותן אמרו להן ב"ש אי אתם מודין במעלה שני שקין מעודדים ונתנן זה על גב זה שהמים יורדין מן העליון לתחתון שהתחתון בכי יותן ר' יוסי אומר אחד שק ואחד שני שקין ב"ש אומרים בכי יותן וב"ה אומרים אינן בכי יותן ר' יהודה אומר ר' אליעזר אומר זה וזה בכי יותן ר' יהושע אומר זה וזה אינן בכי יותן ור"ע אומר התחתון בכי יותן והעליון אינו בכי יותן.

comments.en: but if water is put on the seed and any part of a carcass falls upon it, it shall be unclean for you.
comments.he: וְכִ֤י יֻתַּן־מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־זֶ֔רַע וְנָפַ֥ל מִנִּבְלָתָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם׃ {ס}

sections.en: If one shook a bundle of vegetables and [water] dropped down from the upper [side] to the lower [side]: Bet Shammai say: this comes under the law of ‘if water be put’. But Bet Hillel say: this does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’. Bet Hillel said to Bet Shammai: if one shakes a stalk, do we fear lest water drops from one leaf on the other leaf? Bet Shammai said to them: a stalk is only one, but a bundle has many stalks. Bet Hillel said to them: behold, if one lifted a sack full of produce and put it beside the river, do we fear lest water drops from the upper [side] to the lower [side]? But if he lifted two sacks and placed them one upon the other, the lower [sack] comes under the law of ‘if water be put’. Rabbi Yose says: the lower [sack] remains insusceptible to uncleanness.
sections.he: הַנּוֹעֵר אֲגֻדָּה שֶׁל יָרָק וְיָרְדוּ מִצַּד הָעֶלְיוֹן לַתַּחְתּוֹן, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן. בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים, אֵינָם בְּכִי יֻתַּן. אָמְרוּ בֵית הִלֵּל לְבֵית שַׁמַּאי, וַהֲלֹא הַנּוֹעֵר אֶת הַקֶּלַח, חוֹשְׁשִׁין אָנוּ שֶׁמָּא יָצְאוּ מִן הֶעָלֶה לֶעָלֶה. אָמְרוּ לָהֶן בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, שֶׁהַקֶּלַח אֶחָד, וַאֲגֻדָּה קְלָחִים הַרְבֵּה. אָמְרוּ לָהֶם בֵּית הִלֵּל, הֲרֵי הַמַּעֲלֶה שַׂק מָלֵא פֵרוֹת וּנְתָנוֹ עַל גַּב הַנָּהָר, חוֹשְׁשִׁין אָנוּ שֶׁמָּא יָרְדוּ מִצַּד הָעֶלְיוֹן לַתַּחְתּוֹן. אֲבָל אִם הֶעֱלָה שְׁנַיִם וּנְתָנָן זֶה עַל גַּב זֶה, הַתַּחְתּוֹן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַתַּחְתּוֹן טָהוֹר:

en: כָּרֵישָׁא II, כָּרֵישָׁה m. (see preceding; compare כַּרְשִׁינָה) leek. Shabbat VIII, 5 (80ᵇ) כדי לזבל כ׳ as much manure as is required for one leek plant. Yerushalmi ib. VII, 9ᵈ bottom of page כדי ליטע כרישה as much space as is required for planting one leek. Makhshirin I, 5; Tosefta ib. I, 5.—plural כָּרֵישִׁים, כָּרֵישִׁין. Kilayim I, 2 כ׳ וכְרֵישֵׁי שדה וכ׳ (garden) leek and field-leek … are not heterogeneous, see כִּלְאַיִם. Tosefta Shabbat XV (XVI), 14 גוזזין לו כ׳ ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) (Variant כרשינן) we may cut leek for him (on the Sabbath, as a remedy for a serpent’s bite). Nedarim VI, 9; Tosefta ib. III, 6; Yerushalmi ib. VI, 39ᵈ bottom of page, see קִפְלוֹט; and from—V. כָּרָתֵי.

comments.he: עם זאת, כבר במסכת כלים עמדנו על כך שתנור מטמא אף על פי שהוא מחובר לקרקע, כמו הגולל שבו עסקנו לעיל. טומאת תנור נזכרת במפורש בתורה, וחז"ל לא היו מוכנים כנראה לשנות את הכלל שתנור וכיריים מקבלים טומאה, אף שלפי כללי ההלכה שהם עיצבו בדרך כלל תנור צריך להיות טהור, להוציא תנור שהוא בר טלטול (כלים פ"ה מ"י, וראו פירושנו לה). אם כן, כאן ניכרת הלכה קדומה ביותר (שתנור מטמא).

comments.en: but if water is put on the seed and any part of a carcass falls upon it, it shall be unclean for you.
comments.he: וְכִ֤י יֻתַּן־מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־זֶ֔רַע וְנָפַ֥ל מִנִּבְלָתָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם׃ {ס}

sections.en: If one rubbed a leek or pressed his hair or his garment, Rabbi Yose says: the liquid which came out comes under the law of ‘if water be put’, but the liquid that remained does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’, because his intention was that the liquid should come out of all of it.
sections.he: הַמְמַחֵק אֶת הַכְּרֵישָׁה, וְהַסּוֹחֵט שְׂעָרוֹ בִּכְסוּתוֹ, רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אוֹמֵר, הַיּוֹצְאִין בְּכִי יֻתַּן, וְאֶת שֶׁבּוֹ אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהוּא מִתְכַּוֵּן שֶׁיֵּצְאוּ מִכֻּלּוֹ:

en:
טָמַן (Biblical Hebrew; compare preceding) to hide, store away, preserve, especially to keep dishes warm for the Sabbath. Shabbat II, 7 טוֹמְנִין את החמין you may put warm dishes in the chafing stove &c. Ib. IV, 1; and from—Makhshirin I, 6 הטומן פירותיו וכ׳ if one hides his fruits in water against thieves.—Kohelet Rabbah to X, 8 שהוא ט׳ וכ׳ that he buried it there; and e.—Part. pass. טָמוּן. Bava Kamma 5ᵇ, and e. נזקי ט׳ באש damage caused to things hidden in a pile to which fire was set. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 68 היה ט׳ וכ׳ he (Jacob) was hiding (before Esau) in the house of Eber; Megillah 17ᵃ מוּטְמָן (Manuscript Munich נטמן, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note); and from

Nifal - נִטְמָן to be hidden, to hide one’s self, to be stored up. Ib. שנ׳ בבית עבר, see supra. Vayikra Rabbah section (Parashah) 3 ויִטָּמְנוּ ד"ת בפיך and the words of the Law shall be stored up in thy mouth. Pesikta d'Rav Kahana R. section (Parashah) 4 נ׳ במערה sought protection in a cave; and e.

Hifil - הִטְמִין
1) to hide, keep. Bava Kamma 61ᵇ שדרכם להַטְמִין וכ׳ which it is customary to hide in the stack. Bava Metzia 61ᵇ לא יַטְמִין … במלח he must not keep his weights in salt (by which they gain in weight); and from—Part. pass. מוּטְמָן, see supra.

—2) to hide one’s self, lie in wait. Bava Kamma 79ᵇ ראוהו שה׳ וכ׳ if he has been seen hiding himself in the woods (waiting for a chance to steal).

נָפַח (Biblical Hebrew; compare פּוּחַ)
1) to blow, breathe. Yerushalmi Shabbat VII, 10ᵈ הנוֹפֵח כלי זכוכית he who shapes glass vessels by blowing (on the Sabbath); Bavli Shabbat 75ᵇ המְנַפֵּחַ בכלי וכ׳. Makhshirin I, 6 הנופח בעדשים וכ׳ he who breathes at lentils to ascertain their quality. Tosefta Shabbat XV (XVI), 2 נופח בחוטמו וכ׳ you blow into its nostrils and put the teat into its mouth; Shabbat 128ᵇ; Yerushalmi ib. XVIII, end, 16ᶜ מביא יין ונופח וכ׳ you take wine and squirt it &c. Bava Metzia 60ᵇ אין נוֹפְחִין בקרביים it is not permitted to blow up entrails (for sale, to give them a delusive appearance); and from

—2) to be blown up, to swell. Midrash Tanḥuma K’dosh. 8 נָפְחוּ פניו his face was swollen. Ib. עיניו נְפוּחוֹת his eyes swollen.

Nifal - נִיפֵּחַ same. Shabbat 75ᵇ, see supra. Ma'asrot IV, 5 מְנַפֵּיחַ … ואם ני׳ וכ׳ Yerushalmi ed. (Bavli ed. מנפח … נפח; Manuscript Munich מנפיח; Mishnah ed. מנפה … נפה, see Rabbinowicz Diḳduḳé Sof’rim (Variæ Lectiones &c., Munich 1867-84) and l. note 7) he may blow out (the chaff of the wheat-ears) from hand to hand and eat, but if he blows and puts the grain in his lap, he is bound (to pay tithes); Beitzah 13ᵇ. Ib. 14ᵃ. Berakhot 19ᵇ; Niddah 57ᵃ, and e., see פְּרַס; and from—[Y. Peah VIII, 21ᵇ top המנפח, read המכפח, see קָפַח.]

Pu. - נוּפָּח to be blown, fanned. Masechet Masechet Smachot Chaldaic VIII מוטב … אש שנוּפְּחָה ולא אש שלא נופחה וכ׳ it is better that a fire consume me which has been blown (by man), than a fire that has not been fanned (Gehenna; Job XX, 26).

Nifal - נִיפַּח to be blown up, to swell. Bamidabar Rabbah section (Parashah) 7 תִּנָּפֵחַ כרסי וכ׳ my belly may swell and burst.

סִיקָרִין m. plural (sicarii) murderers, robbers. Makhshirin I, 6 מעשה … מפני הס׳ it happened in Jerusalem that they hid their fig-cakes in water to save them from the robbers (reference. to the terrorists during the last siege of Jerusalem, compare סִיקְרָא III); [Var. lect. סְרִיקִין; R. Hai G. reads: סיקריקין, see next word] Pirkei Avot d’R. N. II, Chaldaic VII (ed. Schechter, p. 20) עמדו כל הס׳ וכ׳ all the terrorists arose and burnt all the provision stores in Jerusalem; (Pirkei Avot d’R. N. I, Chaldaic VII קנאים).

סָרֵיק m. , plural סְרִיקִים, סְרִיקִין (Saf. of רֵק, see סָרַק I) idlers, vagabonds. Midrash Tanḥuma Ki Thetsé 1 שסופו … עם הס׳ וכ׳ for he (the rebellious son) will finally waste his father’s fortune with the vagabonds with whom he eats &c. Sanhedrin 70ᵇ חבורה שכולה ס׳ a company all of which are vagabonds.—Makhshirin I, 6 מפני הס׳ Variant lect., see סִיקָרִין.—[Kiddushin 82ᵃ הסריקים, see סָרוֹק.]—[V. סְרִיקִין.]

שִׁיבּוֹלֶת, שִׁבּוֹ׳, שִׁבֹּלֶת f. (Biblical Hebrew; שבל , Shaf. of יבל; compare יְבוּל)
1) ear of corn, spike. Peah V, 2 ש׳ שבקציר וכ׳ a single ear (that remained uncut when the cutting took place, but) the top of which reached up to the standing corn: if (by its position) it might have been cut with the standing corn &c. Midrash Till. to Psalms II והש׳ בראש הקנה וכ׳ and the ear is on top of the stalk, and its stalk boasts and says, for my sake has the field been sown; and from—Midrash Samuel Chaldaic XX שהיתה שִׁבּוֹלְתָּם גבוהה וכ׳ (not שמלתם) their spikes were as high as those of barley (see עֲנָבָה).—ש׳ שׁוּעָל (fox-tail,) oats. Kilayim I, 1 השעורים וש׳ ש׳ וכ׳ barley and oats … are not considered heterogeneous; (Maimonides: desert (wild) barley). Pesachim II, 5 בחטים … בש׳ ש׳ with unleavened bread made of wheat, barley, spelt, rye, or oats. Ib. 35ᵃ ש׳ ש׳ ושיפון וכ׳ oats and rye are species of barley; ib. ש׳ ש׳ שבולי תעלא Manuscript Oxford (ed. שבילי, correct accordingly) shibboleth shuʿal are (in Chald.) shibbole taʿăla Menachot 70ᵇ; and e.—ש׳ נֵרְדְּ (spica nardi) spikenard, a species of Valerian, an ingredient of frankincense in the Temple. Keritot 6ᵃ; Yerushalmi Yoma IV, 41ᵈ.—ש׳ זָקָן the pointed ends of the chin, the lower jawbones and the chin proper. Makkot 20ᵇ.—plural שִׁבֳּלִים, שִׁבָּלִין, שִׁיבֳּ׳. Shabbat 113ᵇ שתי ש׳ לקטה וכ׳ two ears that fell down she (Ruth) picked up, three, she did not; Yalkut Ruth 601. Tosefta Peah II, 21 השי׳ (ed. Zuckermandel (see Tosefefta) השו׳, correct accordingly); and from

—2) (compare יִבְלָא I) ש׳ הַנָּהָר the current of the river, rapid stream. Makhshirin I, 6 הנותן … בש׳ הנ׳ וכ׳ if a person puts his products on a rapid, that it may float them down. Breishit Rabbah section (Parashah) 56 [read:] לאחד ששמר את גנו מש׳ הנ׳ והקיף גן בנו עמו like one that guarded his garden from the ravages of the current, and surrounded his son’s garden at the same time.

comments.en: but if water is put on the seed and any part of a carcass falls upon it, it shall be unclean for you.
comments.he: וְכִ֤י יֻתַּן־מַ֙יִם֙ עַל־זֶ֔רַע וְנָפַ֥ל מִנִּבְלָתָ֖ם עָלָ֑יו טָמֵ֥א ה֖וּא לָכֶֽם׃ {ס}

sections.en: If one blew on lentils in order to test whether they were good: Rabbi Shimon says: this does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’. But the sages say: this does come under the law of ‘if water be put’. If one ate sesame with his finger, with regard to the liquid that was on his hand: Rabbi Shimon says: this does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’. But the sages say: this does come under the law of ‘if water be put’. If one hid his fruit in water from thieves, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’. Once it happened that the men of Jerusalem hid their fig cakes in water from the robbers, and the sages declared that they were not susceptible to uncleanness. If one put his fruit in the stream of a river to make it come down with him, it does not come under the law of ‘if water be put’.
sections.he: הַנּוֹפֵחַ בַּעֲדָשִׁים לְבָדְקָן אִם יָפוֹת הֵן, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן. וְהָאוֹכֵל שֻׁמְשְׁמִין בְּאֶצְבָּעוֹ, מַשְׁקִין שֶׁעַל יָדוֹ, רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים, בְּכִי יֻתַּן. הַטּוֹמֵן פֵּרוֹתָיו בַּמַּיִם מִפְּנֵי הַגַּנָּבִים, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן. מַעֲשֶׂה בְאַנְשֵׁי יְרוּשָׁלַיִם שֶׁטָּמְנוּ דְבֵלָתָן בַּמַּיִם מִפְּנֵי הַסִּיקָרִין, וְטִהֲרוּ לָהֶן חֲכָמִים. הַנּוֹתֵן פֵּרוֹתָיו בְּשִׁבֹּלֶת הַנָּהָר לַהֲבִיאָן עִמּוֹ, אֵינָן בְּכִי יֻתַּן:
